claims.text: The initial material is a single-crystal, Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy with an equiatomic or near-equiatomic composition.
The initial FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase FCC solid solution.
The initial material is free of precipitates and grain boundaries.
A random distribution of constituent atoms produces severe local lattice distortion in FeNiCrMn.
Uniaxial tensile tests should span approximately 10^-4 to 10^2 s^-1 and 77 to 600 K.
The yield strength of single-crystal FeNiCrMn is weakly or negligibly dependent on strain rate over the proposed regime.
Thermally activated dislocation nucleation at Peierls lattice-friction barriers is the dominant mechanism initiating yield.
Stress-driven dislocation nucleation is not the dominant mechanism initiating yield.
Atomic-size mismatch and local lattice distortion increase Peierls stress and the energy barriers for dislocation nucleation and glide.
At low temperature, thermal activation of dislocation nucleation makes yield stress strongly temperature-dependent but relatively strain-rate-insensitive.
Thermal assistance maintains weak strain-rate sensitivity through 600 K.
Diffusion-controlled dislocation creep becomes dominant only at temperatures substantially above 600 K.
Yield strength decreases strongly as temperature increases.
Post-yield strain hardening is dominated by dislocation glide with possible deformation twinning.
No FCC-to-BCC transformation occurs during initial yielding.
Pure Ni and Cu generally have moderate-to-strong yield-strength strain-rate sensitivity because their lattice friction is lower.
A greater than 10% yield-stress change per decade of strain rate is defined as failure of the strain-rate-insensitivity hypothesis.
Detection of a distinct BCC phase at the onset of yielding would falsify the claim that dislocation nucleation is the primary initial deformation mode.
A strain-rate-sensitivity exponent greater than 0.05 and independent of temperature would indicate dislocation-drag-controlled yielding rather than thermal activation over lattice friction.

contradictions.description: The material is explicitly described as Co-free FeNiCrMn, but the structural mediator attributes its lattice distortion to the size mismatch of Fe, Ni, Cr, Mn, and Co atoms.
